facts.statement: Protiguanodon and Hongshanosaurus are synonyms of Psittacosaurus.
facts.quote: synonyms: *Protiguanodon Osborn, 1923 Hongshanosaurus You, Xu, & Wang, 2003

facts.statement: Psittacosaurus is a genus of extinct ceratopsian dinosaurs known as the "parrot lizard" in Greek.
facts.quote: Psittacosaurus ( ; "parrot lizard" in Greek) is a genus of extinct ceratopsian dinosaur

facts.statement: Psittacosaurus lived between 125 and 105 million years ago.
facts.quote: existing between 125 and 105 million years ago

facts.statement: Psittacosaurus fossils have been found in Asia during the Early Cretaceous period.
facts.quote: from the Early Cretaceous of what is now Asia

facts.statement: Psittacosaurus is the most species-rich non-avian dinosaur genus, with up to 13 known species.
facts.quote: It is notable for being the most species-rich non-avian dinosaur genus. Up to 13 species are known

facts.statement: Adult Psittacosaurus were obligate bipeds characterized by a high skull and a robust beak.
facts.quote: The species of Psittacosaurus were obligate bipeds at adulthood, with a high skull and a robust beak

facts.statement: Researchers suggest Psittacosaurus had complex behaviors based on its brain proportions and size.
facts.quote: Psittacosaurus probably had complex behaviours, based on the proportions and relative size of the brain

facts.statement: Psittacosaurus may have been active during both day and night and possessed well-developed senses of smell and vision.
facts.quote: It may have been active for short periods of time during the day and night, and had well-developed senses of smell and vision

facts.statement: Henry Fairfield Osborn participated in the 1922 Third Asiatic Expedition of the American Museum of Natural History in Mongolia.
facts.quote: In 1922, American paleontologist Henry Fairfield Osborn took part in the Third Asiatic Expedition of the American Museum of Natural History to discover fossils and geologic formations from the Cretaceous and Tertiary of Mongolia

facts.statement: A Mongolian chauffeur named Wong discovered a nearly complete Psittacosaurus skeleton nicknamed the "Red Mesa skeleton".
facts.quote: Wong, the Mongolian chauffeur, discovered a nearly complete skull, jaws, and skeleton of a dinosaur, which was given the nickname of "Red Mesa skeleton"

facts.statement: The holotype specimen AMNH 6254 was described by Osborn in 1924 and named Psittacosaurus mongoliensis.
facts.quote: The specimen, catalogued as AMNH 6254, was described in 1924 by Osborn, only partially prepared, who gave it the name Psittacosaurus mongoliensis

facts.statement: Osborn distinguished Psittacosaurus by its short deep snout, broad rear skull, and lack of teeth in the premaxilla.
facts.quote: Osborn demonstrated the taxon was unique based on the short and deep snout, and the broad rear skull, as well as by lacking teeth in the premaxilla

facts.statement: Osborn established the family Psittacosauridae for Psittacosaurus, hypothesizing a relationship to Ankylosauria.
facts.quote: Osborn created the new family Psittacosauridae for Psittacosaurus, which he considered possibly related to Ankylosauria

facts.statement: William King Gregory suggested that the Protiguanodon specimen might be a juvenile Psittacosaurus based on similarities in size and skull bones.
facts.quote: Gregory suggested in correspondence that the Protiguanodon specimen could represent a juvenile of Psittacosaurus, based on similarities in size, the parietal bones, and the quadrate bones

facts.statement: Yang Zhongjian described two additional Psittacosaurus species in 1932 following discoveries in Inner Mongolia.
facts.quote: Following the discovery of material of psittacosaurids in Haratologay in Inner Mongolia, Yang Zhongjian described two additional species in 1932

facts.statement: Additional material found at the Xinpongnaobao Formation locality included a tooth referred to Protiguanodon and other fragments of uncertain affinity.
facts.quote: An additional tooth, partial hand, and fragments of vertebrae and limbs were found in the same locality, with the tooth being referred to Protiguanodon and the remainder of the material being uncertain

facts.statement: The Oshih locality where Psittacosaurus was found dates to the Early Cretaceous Aptian to Albian age.
facts.quote: The location of discovery is also known as the Oshih locality of the Khukhtek Formation, of Early Cretaceous Aptian to Albian age

facts.statement: Roy Chapman Andrews noted in 1932 that AMNH 6254 was the only high-quality specimen found at the Oshih locality.
facts.quote: It was mentioned in 1932 by American paleontologist Roy Chapman Andrews that AMHN 6254 was the only good specimen that could be found at Oshih

facts.statement: Soviet expeditions to Mongolia between 1946 and 1949 uncovered additional Psittacosaurus fossils.
facts.quote: The Soviet Expeditions into Mongolia from 1946 to 1949 uncovered more material of Psittacosaurus.

facts.statement: A disarticulated specimen of Psittacosaurus mongoliensis was found at the Ulan Osh locality in 1946.
facts.quote: In 1946 they discovered a new locality, Ulan Osh, where a disarticulated specimen of Psittacosaurus mongoliensis was found

facts.statement: In 1948, Soviet expeditions excavated fragmentary postcrania from the Oshih and Ondai Sair sites.
facts.quote: in 1948 they revisited the sites of the American expeditions and excavated fragmentary postcrania from Oshih and Ondai Sair.

facts.statement: Soviet excavations near Kemerovo in Siberia discovered partial skulls and skeletons of multiple Psittacosaurus individuals.
facts.quote: Soviet excavations near Kemerovo in Siberia also discovered a partial skull and skeleton of multiple individuals referrable to Psittacosaurus.

facts.statement: Soviet paleontologist Anatoly Rozhdestvensky described the Kemerovo material in 1955.
facts.quote: This material was described by Soviet paleontologist Anatoly Rozhdestvensky in 1955

facts.statement: In 1958, Yang described multiple Psittacosaurus discoveries from the Qingshan Formation in Laiyang.
facts.quote: In 1958, Yang published a paper on the dinosaurs of Laiyang, in which he described multiple discoveries of Psittacosaurus from a collection of localities of the Qingshan Formation.

facts.statement: Psittacosaurus sinensis was found in a red layer 10 miles northwest of Rongyang City in Shandong.
facts.quote: which was found in a red layer 10 mi northwest of Rongyang City in Shandong.

facts.statement: Yang assigned 11 other specimens to Psittacosaurus sinensis, considering it the most diverse species known at the time.
facts.quote: Yang also assigned 11 other specimens to the taxon, considering it to be the most diverse Psittacosaurus species known at the time.

facts.statement: Psittacosaurus sinensis was distinguished by a shorter and wider snout and a smaller size of 675 mm.
facts.quote: It was distinguished from the other known species by a shorter and wider snout, and an overall smaller size at 675 mm.

facts.statement: Zhao Xijin described further 1958 discoveries from Laiyang in 1962, naming specimen BPV.149 Psittacosaurus youngi.
facts.quote: Further discoveries in the Qingshan Formation of Laiyang in 1958 were described by Zhao Xijin in 1962, giving the new name Psittacosaurus youngi for the specimen BPV.149 in the Beijing Museum of Natural History.

facts.statement: Psittacosaurus youngi is known for a complete skull, partial vertebrae, and partial pelvis, and was distinguished by having the shortest skull, vertebral, and tooth counts among species.
facts.quote: Known for a complete skull, partial vertebral series and partial pelvis, P. youngi was distinguished by Zhao by having the shortest skull of all species, vertebral and tooth counts, and various features of the skull and skeleton.

facts.statement: Later expeditions by Mongolian, Russian, Chinese, American, Polish, Japanese, and Canadian paleontologists recovered Psittacosaurus specimens from Mongolia and northern China.
facts.quote: Many later expeditions by various combinations of Mongolian, Russian, Chinese, American, Polish, Japanese, and Canadian paleontologists also recovered specimens from throughout Mongolia and northern China.

facts.statement: Psittacosaurus mongoliensis fossils are found in strata dating to the Aptian to Albian stages of the Early Cretaceous, approximately 125 to 100 million years ago.
facts.quote: In these areas, Psittacosaurus mongoliensis fossils are found in most sedimentary strata dating to the Aptian to Albian stages of the Early Cretaceous Period, or approximately 125 to 100 mya.

facts.statement: Between nine and eleven species of Psittacosaurus are currently considered valid out of seventeen species that have been referred to the genus.
facts.quote: Seventeen species have been referred to the genus Psittacosaurus, although only nine to eleven are considered valid today.

facts.statement: Psittacosaurus holds the record for the highest number of valid species assigned to any single non-avian dinosaur genus.
facts.quote: This is the highest number of valid species currently assigned to any single non-avian dinosaur.

facts.statement: The species P. sinensis was discovered in the 1950s in the Aptian-Albian Qingshan Formation of Shandong Province, southeast of Beijing.
facts.quote: In the 1950s, a new Chinese species of Psittacosaurus was found in the Aptian-Albian Qingshan Formation of Shandong Province, southeast of Beijing.

facts.statement: C. C. Young named the species P. sinensis to differentiate it from P. mongoliensis, which was originally found in Mongolia.
facts.quote: C. C. Young called it P. sinensis to differentiate it from P. mongoliensis, which had originally been found in Mongolia.

facts.statement: Chinese paleontologist Zhao Xijin named the species P. youngi in 1962 after his mentor, C. C. Young.
facts.quote: Chinese paleontologist Zhao Xijin named a new species after his mentor, C. C. Young, in 1962.

facts.statement: Zhao and Paul Sereno described P. xinjiangensis in 1988, naming it after the Xinjiang Autonomous Region where it was discovered.
facts.quote: In 1988, Zhao and American paleontologist Paul Sereno described P. xinjiangensis, named after the Xinjiang Autonomous Region in which it was discovered.

facts.statement: Several individuals of P. xinjiangensis were discovered in the early 1970s, with the holotype and most complete skeleton belonging to a juvenile.
facts.quote: Several individuals of different ages were discovered in the early 1970s by Chinese paleontologists and described by Sereno and Zhao, although the holotype and most complete skeleton belonged to a juvenile.

facts.statement: Specimens of P. xinjiangensis come from the upper part of the Tugulu Group, which is regarded as Aptian-Albian in age.
facts.quote: These specimens come from the upper part of the Tugulu Group, which is regarded as Aptian-Albian in age.

facts.statement: P. meileyingensis was described in 1988 by Sereno, Zhao, and two Chinese colleagues from the Jiufotang Formation near Meileyingzi in Liaoning Province.
facts.quote: A second species described in 1988 by Sereno and Zhao, along with two Chinese colleagues, was P. meileyingensis from the Jiufotang Formation, near the town of Meileyingzi, Liaoning Province, northeastern China.

facts.statement: P. meileyingensis is known from four fossil skulls and one associated skeleton found in 1973 by Chinese scientists.
facts.quote: This species is known from four fossil skulls, one associated with some skeletal material, found in 1973 by Chinese scientists.

facts.statement: While the age of the Jiufotang Formation in Liaoning is unknown, the neighboring Inner Mongolia province dates it to about 110 Ma in the Albian stage of the Early Cretaceous.
facts.quote: The age of the Jiufotang in Liaoning is unknown, but in the neighbouring province of Inner Mongolia, it has been dated to about 110 Ma, in the Albian stage of the Early Cretaceous.

facts.statement: Eric Buffetaut and Varavudh Suteethorn described P. sattayaraki in 1992 based on a partial jaw from the Aptian-Albian Khok Kruat Formation of Thailand.
facts.quote: French paleontologist Eric Buffetaut and a Thai colleague, Varavudh Suteethorn, described a partial upper and lower jaw from the Aptian-Albian Khok Kruat Formation of Thailand in 1992, giving it the name P. sattayaraki.

facts.statement: Paul Sereno questioned the validity of P. sattayaraki in 2000 due to its eroded and fragmentary nature and lack of characteristic Psittacosaurus features.
facts.quote: In 2000, Sereno questioned the validity of this species, citing its eroded and fragmentary nature, and noted an absence of features characteristic of the genus Psittacosaurus.

facts.statement: In 2002, the original authors of P. sattayaraki published new images showing teeth with a bulbous vertical ridge characteristic of psittacosaurs, defending the species' validity.
facts.quote: However, in 2002 the original authors published new images of the fossil which seem to show teeth in the lower jaw that exhibit the bulbous vertical ridge characteristic of psittacosaurs.

facts.statement: In 2010, Paul Sereno proposed that the type material of P. sattayaraki might best be assigned to Ceratopsia incertae sedis.
facts.quote: Sereno (2010) proposed that the best assignment for the type material may be Ceratopsia incertae sedis.

facts.statement: Dale Russell and Zhao described two new species of Psittacosaurus in 1996.
facts.quote: Two new species of Psittacosaurus were described by Canadian Dale Russell and Zhao in 1996.

facts.statement: P. neimongoliensis was named after Inner Mongolia and is based on a nearly complete skeleton found in the Early Cretaceous Ejinhoro Formation along with seven other individuals.
facts.quote: The first was named P. neimongoliensis, after the Mandarin Chinese name for Inner Mongolia. It is based on a nearly complete fossil skeleton, including most of the skull, found in the Early Cretaceous Ejinhoro Formation with seven other individuals.

facts.statement: P. ordosensis was named in 1996 after the Ordos prefecture of the Inner Mongolia Autonomous Region.
facts.quote: Russell and Zhao also named P. ordosensis in 1996, after the Ordos prefecture of the Inner Mongolia Autonomous Region.

facts.statement: P. ordosensis was discovered in the Ejinhoro Formation, the same formation as P. neimongoliensis.
facts.quote: Like P. neimongoliensis, this species was discovered in the Eijnhoro Formation.

facts.statement: Paul Sereno found P. ordosensis indistinguishable from P. sinensis in 2010 but suggested further study might reveal diagnostic features.
facts.quote: Sereno (2010) found the species as described to be indistinguishable from P. sinensis, another small species, but suggested that additional study of P. ordosensis might reveal diagnostic features.

facts.statement: In 1997, Chinese paleontologist Xu Xing named the species P. mazongshanensis based on a complete skull, vertebrae, and a forelimb.
facts.quote: Xu Xing, another Chinese paleontologist, named a new species of Psittacosaurus in 1997, based on a complete skull with associated vertebrae and a forelimb.

facts.statement: Remains of P. mazongshanensis were found in the Lower Xinminbao Formation, with evidence suggesting deposition in the late Barremian through Aptian stages.
facts.quote: The remains were found in the Lower Xinminbao Formation, which have not been precisely dated, although there is some evidence that they were deposited in the late Barremian through Aptian stages.

facts.statement: In 2000, Sereno suggested that P. mazongshanensis is a nomen dubium because it lacks unique features separating it from other Psittacosaurus species.
facts.quote: Sereno suggested in 2000 that P. mazongshanensis was a nomen dubium, with no unique features that separate it from any other species of Psittacosaurus.

facts.statement: Starting in the 1950s, Russian paleontologists excavated Psittacosaurus remains near Shestakovo village in Kemerovo Oblast, Western Siberia.
facts.quote: P. sibiricus Beginning in the 1950s, Russian paleontologists began excavating Psittacosaurus remains at a locality near Shestakovo village in Kemerovo Oblast in Western Siberia.

facts.statement: P. sibiricus was named in 2000 by five Russian paleontologists, with official credit given to Alexei Voronkevich and Alexander Averianov.
facts.quote: This species was named P. sibiricus in 2000 in a scientific paper written by five Russian paleontologists, but credit for the name is officially given to two of those authors, Alexei Voronkevich and Alexander Averianov.

facts.statement: Specimens of P. sibiricus from the Ilek Formation of Siberia date to the Barremian to Aptian stages of the Early Cretaceous.
facts.quote: Two nearly complete, articulated skeletons and a variety of disarticulated material from other individuals of all ages are known from the Ilek Formation of Siberia, which ranges from the Barremian to Aptian stages of the Early Cretaceous.

facts.statement: Individuals of P. sibiricus could reach a length of 2.5 meters, making it one of the largest species in the genus.
facts.quote: Individuals of this species could grow up to 2.5 m in length, making it one of the largest members of the genus.

facts.statement: Revised dating methods indicate that the lower beds of the Yixian Formation containing P. lujiatunensis are approximately 123 million years old.
facts.quote: While this bed has been dated differently by different authors, from 128 Ma in the Barremian stage, to 125 Ma in the earliest Aptian, revised dating methods have shown them to be about 123 million years old.

facts.statement: Sereno (2010) considered P. lujiatunensis and H. houi separate species due to inadequacies in the type specimen of H. houi, despite potential synonymy.
facts.quote: It is potentially synonymous with H. houi; Sereno (2010), who proposed that Hongshanosaurus is a synonym of Psittacosaurus, opted to leave P. lujiatunensis and H. houi separate species due to the inadequacies of the latter's type specimen.

facts.statement: The species H. houi was first described in 2003 as the first named Lujiatun psittacosaur.
facts.quote: A third species of Lujiatun psittacosaur, the first to be named, was described as Hongshanosaurus houi in 2003.

facts.statement: The generic name Hongshanosaurus is derived from the Chinese words for 'red' and 'hill' combined with the Greek word for 'lizard'.
facts.quote: The generic name Hongshanosaurus was derived from the Mandarin Chinese words 紅 (hóng: "red") and 山 (shān: "hill"), as well as the Greek word sauros ("lizard").

facts.statement: Sereno (2010) argued that distinct proportions in Hongshanosaurus skulls were due to crushing and compression, suggesting it is a junior synonym of Psittacosaurus.
facts.quote: Sereno (2010) regarded its distinct proportions as due to crushing and compression of the Hongshanosaurus skulls. He regarded Hongshanosaurus as a junior synonym of Psittacosaurus, and potentially the same as P. lujiatunensis.

facts.statement: P. gobiensis is known from a skull and a partial articulated skeleton containing gastroliths.
facts.quote: It is known from a skull and partial articulated skeleton with gastroliths.

facts.statement: Nearly 100 Psittacosaurus skeletons were excavated in Mongolia in 2005 and 2006 by a team led by Bolortsetseg Minjin and Jack Horner.
facts.quote: Nearly 100 Psittacosaurus skeletons were excavated in Mongolia during the summers of 2005 and 2006 by a team led by Mongolian paleontologist Bolortsetseg Minjin and American Jack Horner from the Museum of the Rockies in Montana.

facts.statement: The specimen of P. amitabha is one of the few vertebrate fossils from the Andakhuduk Formation, which dates to the Barremian stage of the early Cretaceous.
facts.quote: This specimen is one of the few vertebrate fossils known from the Andakhuduk Formation, which dates to the Barremian stage of the early Cretaceous period.

facts.statement: The best-known species, P. mongoliensis, could reach a length of 2 meters (6.5 feet).
facts.quote: The best-known—P. mongoliensis—can reach 2 metres (6.5 ft) in length.

facts.statement: The maximum adult body weight of P. mongoliensis was likely over 20 kilograms (44 pounds).
facts.quote: The maximum adult body weight was most likely over 20 kilogrammes (44 lb) in P. mongoliensis.

facts.statement: Psittacosaurus had four digits on its hand, unlike the five found in most other ornithischians.
facts.quote: There are only four digits on the manus ('hand'), as opposed to the five found in most other ornithischians

facts.statement: The portion of the skull in front of the eye socket was only 40% of the total skull length, which is shorter than in any other known ornithischian.
facts.quote: The portion in front of the orbit (eye socket) is only 40% of total skull length, shorter than any other known ornithischian.

facts.statement: The lower jaws of Psittacosaurus were characterized by a bulbous vertical ridge down the center of each tooth.
facts.quote: The lower jaws of psittacosaurs are characterised by a bulbous vertical ridge down the centre of each tooth.

facts.statement: Psittacosaurus fossils date to the Early Cretaceous period.
facts.quote: fossil_range: Cretácico Inferior

facts.statement: Psittacosaurus lived during the Early Cretaceous, between 130 and 100 million years ago, from the Barremian to the Aptian.
facts.quote: que vivieron a mediados del período Cretácico Inferior, entre 130 a 100 millones de años, desde el Barremiano hasta el Aptiano

facts.statement: Psittacosaurus lived in what is now Asia.
facts.quote: en lo que hoy es Asia

facts.statement: Fossils of at least 14 species have been found in regions of modern China, Mongolia, and Russia, with a possible additional species in Thailand.
facts.quote: Se han identificado por lo menos 14 especies de fósiles encontrados en diversas regiones de lo que hoy en día es China, Mongolia y Rusia, con una posible especie adicional en Tailandia.

facts.statement: All species of Psittacosaurus were gazelle-sized, bipedal herbivores with a high and powerful beak on the upper jaw.
facts.quote: Todas las especies de Psittacosaurus tenían el tamaño de una gacela, eran bípedos herbívoros con un alto y poderoso pico en la mandíbula superior.

facts.statement: At least one species had long tube-like bristle structures on its tail and lower back, which likely served for display.
facts.quote: Al menos una de estas especies tenía largas estructuras similares a cerdas tubulares en su cola y espalda baja, que probablemente sirvieran en la exhibición.

facts.statement: Psittacosaurus likely had complex behaviors based on the proportions and relative size of its brain.
facts.quote: Psittacosaurus probablemente tenía comportamientos complejos, basados en las proporciones y el tamaño relativo del cerebro.

facts.statement: It is possible that Psittacosaurus was active during brief periods of both day and night and had well-developed senses of smell and vision.
facts.quote: Es posible que haya estado activo durante breves períodos de tiempo durante el día y la noche, y tenga los sentidos del olfato y la visión bien desarrollados.

facts.statement: More than 400 individuals, including many complete specimens, have been collected.
facts.quote: Se han recolectados fósiles de más de 400 individuos, incluyendo muchos ejemplares completos.

facts.statement: The genus Psittacosaurus was named by Osborn in 1923.
facts.quote: genus_authority: Osborn, 1923

facts.statement: Psittacosaurus belongs to the family Psittacosauridae.

facts.statement: Protiguanodon is a synonym of Psittacosaurus.
facts.quote: synonyms: * Protiguanodon Osborn, 1923

facts.statement: While Psittacosaurus is less familiar to the public than its distant relative Triceratops, it is one of the most complete dinosaurs known.
facts.quote: Psittacosaurus no es tan familiar en el público en general como su pariente distante Triceratops pero es uno de los más completos dinosaurios conocidos.

facts.statement: The species with the most data, Psittacosaurus mongoliensis, could reach up to 2 meters in length.
facts.quote: La especie de la que se dispone un mayor número de datos e información, Psittacosaurus mongoliensis, podía alcanzar hasta 2 metros de longitud.

facts.statement: The maximum body weight of an adult P. mongoliensis probably exceeded 20 kilograms.
facts.quote: El peso máximo del cuerpo de un P. mongoliensis adulto superaba probablemente los 20 kilogramos.

facts.statement: P. ordosensis is the smallest known species, with a size 30% smaller than that of P. mongoliensis.
facts.quote: El P. ordosensis es la especie más pequeña conocida, con un tamaño un 30 % menor que el del P. mongoliensis.

facts.statement: The postcranial skeletons of Psittacosaurus are more typical of a generic bipedal ornithischian.
facts.quote: Los esqueletos postcraneales de Psittacosaurus son más típicos de un ornitisquio bípedo "genérico".

facts.statement: The skull of Psittacosaurus shows many modifications compared to other ornithischian dinosaurs, being extremely high, short, and with a rounded profile in some species.
facts.quote: El cráneo de Psittacosaurus presenta muchas modificaciones en comparación con otros dinosaurios ornitisquios, siendo extremadamente alto, corto y con un perfil redondo en algunas especies.

facts.statement: As the generic name suggests, the short skull superficially resembles that of parrots.
facts.quote: Como el nombre genérico sugiere, el cráneo corto recuerda superficialmente al de los loros.

facts.statement: P. sibiricus possessed bony horns protruding from the skull, but these are likely an example of convergent evolution.
facts.quote: P. sibiricus poseyó cuernos óseos que resaltaban del cráneo, pero éstos son probablemente un ejemplo de evolución convergente.

facts.statement: In P. mongoliensis, as in other species, the length of the forelimbs was 58% of the hindlimbs, suggesting these animals were bipedal throughout their lives.
facts.quote: En P. mongoliensis, al igual que en otras especies, la longitud de los miembros delanteros era de un 58 % respecto a la longitud de los miembros traseros, por lo que se deduce que estos animales manifestaban una locomoción bípeda a lo largo de toda su vida.

facts.statement: The parent group of Psittacosaurus is Ceratopsia.
facts.quote: Parent group: Ceratopsia

facts.statement: Psittacosaurus belongs to the class Ornithischia.
facts.quote: Class: Ornithischia

facts.statement: Psittacosaurus lived from the Valanginian to the Albian stages, between 137.05 and 100.5 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Valanginian to Albian (137.05 to 100.5 million years ago)

facts.statement: Li et al. (2026) described ornithischian fossil material from the Lower Cretaceous Bayin-Gobi Formation in China, representing the westernmost record of a dinosaur similar to Psittacosaurus reported to date.
facts.quote: Ornithischian fossil material including caudal vertebrae with similarities to the vertebrae of Psittacosaurus, representing the westernmost record of a dinosaur from the Lower Cretaceous Bayin-Gobi Formation (China) reported to date, is described by Li et al. (2026).
